title: Non-search engine audit
scope: Rules, legal/pseudo-legal generation, board and move representations, state application/simulation, hashes, draw/lifecycle machinery and agent-facing interchange. Search algorithms, move ordering/pruning, evaluation formulas, neural inference and training were excluded. Cache lifecycle at state boundaries was included.
headline: Targeted allocation and generation improvements are plausible; narrow state/interchange bugs are reproduced. No integrated engine or playing-strength gain is established.
method: First-pass screen on Intel i7-1255U Linux x86_64, rustc 1.92.0 / LLVM 21.1.3, release ThinLTO and one codegen unit, default portable CPU target, taskset CPU 2. Baseline and candidate helpers run in the same executable with black_box; most timing groups alternate arm order. Repetitions are batch means, not individual latency quantiles. CPU frequency/background load were not controlled; these are pilot measurements with ranges, not formal confidence intervals. Packing, prebuilt geometry construction, and mutation overhead are excluded where specified. Baseline production revision is the SHA above; candidate identity is the named example plus its recorded content hash.

inventory.coverage: Square lookup, per-color dense lists, slot indices, swap removal, royal/global masks, heap versus inline arrays, SoA, packed pieces.
Standard/two-step/Free Eagle shape, full victim identity, inline paths, Copy specialization, u64 packing, wire compatibility.
Square arithmetic, next-square and ray tables, delta geometry, mailbox sentinels, line occupancy, bitscans, magic/PEXT scaling.
Simple/range/jump/conditional patterns, origin-sensitive promotion forms, perpendicular second legs, overlays, count/any/stream APIs.
Dedup sort/bitmap choices, tiny-list overhead, ordering, raw multiplicity, capture-mode specialization, route coalescing.
Directed probes, cached metadata, local/global attacker masks, virtual attacker scans, eager attack caches and independent rule checks.
Checked/trusted application, transactionality, path captures including friendly sweeps, make/unmake, hash parity and promotion.
Royal capture, progress clock, repeated positions, prefix caches, insufficient material, reset/restore/edit invariants.
BoardPosition/JSON, TSFEN/TM1, legacy records, UCI admission, session snapshots, timeline cloning and replay.
Enum/niche/layout facts, Copy versus Clone, fixed/static descriptors, OnceLock, allocation reuse, LTO/native/unsafe tradeoffs.

findings.title: Use allocation census to target remaining temporary storage
findings.finding: Warmed opening generation returns 280 moves with 105 allocation/reallocation calls and 34120 total requested bytes. Reusing its final Vec reduces this to 97 calls and 1480 requested bytes: intermediate storage remains. Captures-only returns 80 moves with 44 calls. This identifies a real allocation budget for streamed targets and inline paths.
findings.limits: One opening fixture; requested allocation bytes are cumulative, not live/peak memory. Global allocator instrumentation was used for counts, not latency claims. The genuine quiet make/unmake and quiet delta construction each allocate zero; do not optimize imaginary per-quiet capture allocations.

findings.title: Use168-byte square bitmap for large/duplicate-heavy final target unions
findings.finding: Dedup-only paired median speedups3.23–8.78x on tested duplicate-rich Lion/Tengu/HookMover/FE lists. Empty Rook2.48x; sparse Rook2.75x. Exact final vectors agree. Empty Hook raw2590 ->1295unique: stable-sort median35.88us vs bitmap4.04us. Empty Tengu raw1294 ->647unique:16.34us vs1.90us.
findings.limits: Pawn~2.3xslower and dense3targetRook~1.6xslower. Need adaptive policy and integrated generator timing. Bitmap target union cannot replace complete route identity.

findings.title: Restrict bent-slider second leg before walking it
findings.finding: Full second fanout is generated before perpendicular-continuation rejection. Prototype masks second directions to two perpendicular rays. Through an empty first corner, these rays never touch old mover square or corner, so original Board lookup suffices. 1152 ordered-list parity cases passed:4seeds x3densities x4origins x6source families x2colors xactual promotions. Final Cargo-built measurements are in the measurement appendix; initial standalone rustc timings are archived separately.
findings.limits: Combined masking+overlay-removal. Current RangeRange NoJump semantics only; complete legal Move builder needs separate route, promotion/progress-state tests and integration timing. Candidate fallback handles other capabilities but optimization proof is narrow.

findings.title: Inline Free Eagle routes in Move
findings.finding: One Vec-containing MoveData variant inflates every standard and two-step move and each Free Eagle route clone allocates. Current generator routes fit five Positions including origin. An inline enum with [Position;5] and u8 length preserves full route identity, return captures and path order. The final Copy inline representation is 17 B versus 32 B current Move. Opening clone control with Clone only was 3.70x slower, while identical Copy storage cloned much faster. Smaller layout alone is insufficient; Copy enables bulk copying.
findings.limits: This is a storage/clone prototype, not integrated generator or execution performance. Public MoveData serde currently accepts arbitrary Vec lengths; production conversion needs validation or a large-route fallback and stable serialization. Whole move generation, copying and agent throughput still need measurement. A generic SmallVec with heap fallback may itself keep a pointer-sized union and expand the Move; validate actual size rather than substituting it automatically.

findings.title: Borrow armies for insufficient-material checks
findings.finding: is_draw_by_insufficient_material clones both armies before any early rejection. Existing borrowed slices permit the identical nonempty/all predicate without allocation or copy. In the initial position this removes two copies of 402 Pieces even though the first disqualifying piece is sufficient.
findings.limits: A useful per-call cleanup; no whole-agent speedup claimed. A maintained nonqualifying-material count could make late-game checks O(1), but adds mutation invariants and was not implemented.

findings.title: Borrow armies when producing BoardPosition snapshots
findings.finding: from_state calls clone-returning get_pieces_by_color four times: two clones only to obtain lengths, then two clones feeding a final owned Vec. Borrow lengths and extend_from_slice into the single required snapshot Vec.
findings.limits: Benefits serialization/snapshot production; this path need not dominate agent play. Existing piece order and public serde shape can be preserved exactly.

findings.title: Bulk-load validated snapshots and hash once
findings.finding: Bulk snapshot loading eliminates repeated full-board hashing. BoardPosition::to_state at src/board_position.rs:85-96 calls GameState::place_piece for every piece; place_piece at src/game_state.rs:600-605 recomputes the entire current board hash and reseeds repetition each time. This is quadratic in snapshot size. The equivalent prototype validates once, places into Board directly, then calls restore_position once. The full 804-piece opening matched every square and final hash. Revised 8 rounds x300 loads with 30 warmups/method and alternating order measured median batch means 489,923.59 ns/current versus 6,424.86 ns/bulk per load, a 76.25x ratio or 98.69% reduction. Current round means ranged 478,988.82-525,111.31 ns; bulk ranged 6,247.30-13,028.44 ns. These are repeated-batch means, not individual-request tail latencies or independent statistical confidence intervals. This is snapshot loading only, not whole-game or search throughput. Implementation is small; retain validation and one canonical hash/repetition reset.

findings.title: Free Eagle history omits the final leg
findings.finding: FreeEagle generated moves omit the final leg in in-engine history. src/game_state.rs:2048-2058 intentionally skips the final entry when path[i]==mv.to, and the following condition also skips it because path.last()==mv.to. Generated one-leg path history length is 0; generated two-, three-, four-leg path histories have lengths 1, 2, 3. This is reproducible for actual generated moves, with no malformed input. Any consumer of GameState::get_move_history gets incomplete history; evaluate() currently derives default ply from history length, while external GameHistory records are independent. Fix final-leg recording and decide explicitly whether this API counts logical turns or physical legs (TwoStep currently records both legs). Avoid silently changing both semantics in one patch.

findings.title: Check promotion flags at external move admission
findings.finding: Promotion validation is incomplete at public-input boundaries. make_move documents an assumption that the caller validated, yet invokes apply_move(validate=true), and UCI position-moves invokes it directly as the legality gate. execute_single_move at src/game_state.rs:2167-2174 trusts mv.promoted. Probes demonstrate: Pawn 8,8->8,9+ promotes outside the zone even though not generated; Pawn 8,34->8,35 without + declines compulsory promotion even though not generated; an already Pawn-promoted GoldGeneral promotes again to Rook, retains base Pawn and makes BoardPosition::validate reject the resulting state; a King move carrying + leaves the King unpromoted but resets progress clock 99->0. These are malformed-external-move cases; normal generated moves passed parity checks. Centralize promotion eligibility, compulsory promotion and actual promotion outcome validation in checked application. Keep the trusted generated-move fast contract separate so checking does not slow every agent-generated move. Prioritize external UCI/import correctness rather than calling generated movement broken.
findings.limits: External malformed-input findings are separate from generated-move consistency; ordinary generated samples passed.

findings.title: Invalidate position-dependent caches when restoring snapshots
findings.finding: restore_position retains stale evaluator caches. src/game_state.rs:644 replaces board/turn/draw/history/hash/repetition but does not clear eval_inc or nnue, unlike clear_board/place_piece. Probe initializes EvalInc on a Pawn board, restores an empty board, calls ensure_eval_inc with the same weights, and confirms the retained cache differs from fresh EvalInc::from_board. Current production debug rebuild callsites create GameState::new first, limiting immediate impact. Still a real public-method invariant violation; clear the two caches in restore_position. NNUE issue is source-derived, not separately runtime reproduced.

findings.title: Reject malformed legacy game coordinates before formatting
findings.finding: Legacy GameRecord formatting bypasses checked coordinates. GameHistory::record_to_move at src/game_history.rs:229 checks u8 coordinate values via Position::new; GameHistory::load_game at line368 deserializes raw records without validation, and format_game at lines640-641 and906 unwraps Position::new. The revised catch_unwind probe supplies from_file=255; both checked-converter rejection and formatter panic are confirmed true. This is malformed-file robustness, not generated-record corruption. The CLI invokes format_game at src/main.rs:686. Reuse checked conversion and report a readable error rather than panic.
findings.limits: External malformed-input findings are separate from generated-move consistency; ordinary generated samples passed.

findings.title: Avoid Free Eagle list regeneration during trusted application
findings.finding: Normalize FreeEagle internal representation before trusted application. apply_move at src/game_state.rs:1893-1905 regenerates the full FreeEagle move list whenever a FreeEagle move is not MoveData::FreeEagle, even with validate=false. The move generator emits Standard range moves for FreeEagles (lines2558-2580), so those generated trusted applications can reenter full generation. With validate=true, a Standard that becomes a path generates the list twice: once for endpoint normalization, once for .contains validation at line2008. examples/audit_free_eagle_probe.rs measured an endpoint-identical generated Standard and one-leg FreeEagle capturing path on a two-piece fixture; all square contents, final hash and progress clock matched, and undo restored canonical hash. Five alternating rounds x10,000 repetitions after100 warmups/method: trusted Standard make+unmake median batch mean 3,008.43 ns versus trusted explicit path 73.00 ns (~41.21x); clone+validated Standard make median 6,642.45 ns versus clone+validated explicit path 3,615.01 ns (~1.84x). No search ran. This isolates representation/normalization overhead and demonstrates waste; it is not a claimed whole-engine speedup. Store a canonical route or execute the explicitly generated Standard range route directly after establishing equivalent capture semantics. Direct external path geometry validation could avoid the remaining full list generation. External destination-only compatibility normalization can choose a route and must be preserved or deliberately changed.
findings.limits: Same endpoints can have different route victims. The microfixture deliberately matches final board/hash; any implementation must preserve the current Standard normalization route, rather than blindly choosing an arbitrary explicit path. No integrated runtime gain measured.

findings.title: Repair documented Free Eagle TM1 syntax and identity
findings.finding: TM1 generated FreeEagle identity does not always round-trip, while documented tokens have a more serious separate issue. src/notation.rs:95/104 appends a full path (which generated FreeEagle paths start with origin) after already appending from. A one-leg FreeEagle becomes from-from-to, and decoder length3 constructs TwoStep (lines143-147). Eight of165 opening-empty-board FreeEagle moves had Move identity mismatches, zero execution rejection, zero final-board mismatch because apply_move renormalizes non-path FreeEagles by destination. Do not claim board corruption from those eight identity-only mismatches. HOWEVER src/README.md:65 documents FreeEagle as from + path with no repeated origin, e.g. 12,3-13,4-14,5-15,6. Decoding such a >=3-leg token gives a FreeEagle path excluding from; checked apply compares exact generated paths which include from, so the documented syntax is rejected. examples/audit_notation_probe.rs was compiled with rustc against the current release rlib and executed. Exact token18,18-19,19-20,20-21,21 decoded successfully, checked application rejected it with no board/hash mutation, while the generated equivalent path including origin applied and captured the Pawn at19,19. Output: benchmarks/non_search_engine_20261101/notation.txt. Canonical typed syntax/explicit path convention should resolve both without breaking the JSON canonical persistence format.

findings.title: Rank/file/diagonal occupancy words
findings.finding: Each36-square line fitsu64.36 ranks+36files+71diagonals+71antidiagonals=214 words=1712 bytes per chosen occupancy set; nearest blockers can use masks plus trailing/leading_zeros. This is the scalable part of chess sliding attack techniques. Root prototype passed 31,104 ordinary-rook count comparisons across 12 synthetic boards; rows/files use 1152 B. The kernel improves all tested densities, but excludes updates, construction, route effects, diagonals and Move emission.
findings.limits: Mutators must update four line words per change, virtual board deltas need correct overlays, and capturing rays need blocker-class distinctions. No full engine performance claim from nearest-blocker kernels.

findings.title: Reuse specialized target probes in generic exported multileg reach API
findings.finding: 134784 specialized/generated checks pass. Existing specialized kernels25–920x faster than generic generate-and-contains on tested directed queries.
findings.limits: Board attack dispatcher ALREADY uses specialized kernels. Standard validation probes first leg; explicit two-step validation probes individual legs. Existing workflow impact may be small. Do not label25–920x as legal-generation or engine speedup.

findings.title: Extend existing visitor/append/count design into nested multi-leg generation
findings.finding: Common Simple/Range/Jumping already append directly. Multi-leg still allocates first list and every second list. Short-circuit visitor can serve count/any/union/caller output.
findings.limits: No integrated timing. Existing dyn BoardLike in first-leg overlay intentionally avoids recursive generic-type explosion.

findings.title: Replace White eight-branch direction permutation with u8.rotate_left(4)
findings.finding: All256 masks agree with production for512 color checks plus256 copied-body checks. Cargo release rustc1.92.0 x86-64 exported frozen bodies emit11 versus3 instructions including ret (10 versus2 excluding ret). Reproducible source examples/audit_direction_probe.rs; complete compiler/parity/assembly metadata benchmarks/non_search_engine_20261101/direction-rotation.json. cargo clippy --example audit_direction_probe -- -D warnings passed without allow attributes.
findings.limits: Assembly only, no workflow gain measured. Cached filters already avoid much recomputation.

findings.title: Replace remaining fixed direction Vecs with arrays/iterators
findings.finding: Hot general walkers already use allocation-free direction_iter, but Free Eagle generation builds Vecs for two forward directions, six others and Direction::all; generator's Free Eagle fallback also calls Direction::all. Fixed arrays preserve order and remove these small heap allocations. In the target-only Free Eagle fallback, an additional path Vec is written but never read; remove it only there. Legal Free Eagle route generation still needs its actual paths.
findings.limits: Existing direction-bits historical screen was already accepted/current. This item concerns residual fixed-size Vec sites, not reapplying that existing optimization. Cold candidate mask table initialization allocations are low priority.

findings.title: Return explicit move-application success and errors
findings.finding: Make move success explicit in the API. src/game_state.rs:1746 returns None for both successful Standard/FreeEagle moves and failure; only TwoStep success returns Some(intermediate). Multiple callers detect a side-to-move flip as an auxiliary success signal. A Result<AppliedMove, MoveError> with optional intermediate is clearer, permits useful failures and transactional input handling. This is an API cleanup/correctness enabler; speed unmeasured. Existing caller logic is often correct, so the ambiguity alone is not evidence those callers mishandle a move.

findings.title: Unused VirtualBoard composition loses distinct earlier movers
findings.finding: Generic VirtualBoard::compose is not a trustworthy new optimization primitive. At src/move_simulation.rs:168-200, a second move by a distinct piece overwrites the sole piece_moved slot. Probe moves a Black King then a White King; the first original remains and its destination vanishes, while only the second move is represented. rg finds no production compose callsites. Fix/remove/document restriction before any future use; low immediate priority because unused. Do not base nested-move optimization claims on it.

findings.title: Avoid full timeline cloning for small session views
findings.finding: DebugTool::recorded_evals only needs records at cursor-1 and cursor, but effective_moves constructs an owned clone of the full timeline. snapshot also allocates display strings for every piece; the opening snapshot used 3274 allocator/reallocator calls and 288438 cumulative requested bytes. Borrow selected records or stream timeline segments when GUI polling makes this material.
findings.limits: Most allocation calls are expected presentation strings. No isolated latency attribution or production agent-throughput benefit measured. Snapshot already reuses its computed check and legal-move count in status_summary_with; do not reintroduce duplicate work.

findings.title: Precompute adjacent-square or full ray tables
findings.finding: A next-square table [1296][8] of u16 needs20736 bytes with sentinel; full directed ray-square lists contain150360 squares, about300720 bytes before offsets. They replace repeated coordinate bounds arithmetic with table reads.
findings.limits: Additional L1/L2 traffic may outweigh arithmetic; current candidate masks already occupy217728 bytes. Test next-square table separately before committing large full-ray tables; preserve variable-distance and jumping/capturing rules.

findings.title: Padded mailbox board
findings.finding: 38x38 with sentinel border uses1444 squares,11.4% more than1296, and allows local step increments plus offboard sentinel.64-wide stride makes file/rank bit operations cheaper but at least64x38 uses2432 slots,87.7% larger.
findings.limits: Long jumps require enough sentinel padding or explicit checks; 0x88 chess masks do not directly represent36 files. Coordinate/serde translation and move ordering complicate migration. No evidence yet that offset bounds branches dominate.

findings.title: Batch common short movers using masks
findings.finding: SF/YaneuraOu batch pawn shifts may transfer to common short-move classes.1296bits=21words, crossword carries/full scan may lose vs army lists or per-line masks. Not timed.

findings.title: Compile shared movement signatures
findings.finding: Compile per shared movement signature/color rather than each303types: static offsets/masks or specialized common handlers. Trade setup/enum interpretation against instruction-cache size. Existing metadata caches cover much already.

findings.title: Directed Wooden Dove reach probe
findings.finding: Wooden Dove direct probe determines diagonal/distance and tests just necessary path/destination. Existing full4direction generation avoidable. Current configs onlybase3,conditional4/5; not timed separately.

findings.title: Specialize capture and blocker modes outside ray loops
findings.finding: Like SF/YaneuraOu generation templates, specialize captures_only and blocking mode outside ray loops. Compiler may unswitch already; inspect assembly and benchmark before multiplying code.

findings.title: Small coordinate-difference geometry table
findings.finding: 71x71coordinate-difference direction/distance table (~5041entries) rather than1296²square-pair table. Current direct algebra already small; extra load may lose. Not timed.

findings.title: Skip target union dedup for proved-disjoint capabilities
findings.finding: Precompute overlap/disjointness to skip dedup for simple cases. Preserve final file-major order and raw duplicate compatibility; bitmap adaptive policy may be simpler.

findings.title: Directed Free Eagle reach probe
findings.finding: FreeEagle target checks need not generate+sort all patterns. Ordinary clear range already short-circuits; enemy chain/special returns still fan out. Test every return pattern and route victim set.

findings.title: Expand independent movement-rule checks
findings.finding: New checks and existing broad movement audits share configs. Hand-derived family cases, physically updated first legs, color/blocker metamorphisms and progression parity improve independent correctness evidence; no new rule bug established here.

findings.title: Reuse or inline short target scratch buffers
findings.finding: Inline capacity/reused scratch for short targets; measure cardinality distribution and recursive ownership. Never size per-frame stack storage for largest fanout.

findings.title: Stream immediate capturing-ray victim walks
findings.finding: Stream capturing-ray victims via iterator/callback when path list only feeds immediate remove/visit. APIs exposing complete routes still need storage; scope individual callsites.

findings.title: Flatten movement descriptors and intern blocker sets
findings.finding: MovementCapability embeds a5-word PieceTypeSet in its largest Range variant, inflating every capability; Jumping/conditional offsets allocate Vecs and TwoStep boxes child descriptors. Interning the few blocker sets via a small id, using static slices, and flattening child indices could make descriptors more cache-friendly. The measured current enum size is48 bytes; its five-word blocker set contributes40 bytes. Any smaller descriptor size remains a source-derived hypothesis until compiled.
findings.limits: Configs are initialized once and borrowed, so this mainly saves global table footprint/cold initialization and cache loads, not per-move allocations. Keep current semantics for origin-sensitive Whale and RainDragon. Needs config walk/movegen profile before a major rewrite.

findings.title: Compile-time movement/config tables instead of per-entry OnceLock
findings.finding: for_piece_type uses an array of303 OnceLocks. After warmup it returns shared configs without cloning or mutex locks; a static flattened table could remove acquire checks and heap-built descriptors.
findings.limits: Startup wins and steady-state wins differ. Current initialization cost is amortized, and incorrect origin/type dispatch would break special movement. Do not describe current table as a hot HashMap or per-call allocation.

findings.title: Pack complete moves into u64
findings.finding: 1296 squares need11 bits. Source plus up to four route landings requires55 bits; kind2, length3 and promotion1 fit61 bits. Two-step needs source/via/dest33 bits. Prototype retains route order and origin-returning captures, unlike endpoint-only compression.
findings.limits: Decode/index conversion overhead, public API changes, invalid-bit validation, future longer routes and serde compatibility are unmeasured. Start with inline representation if it captures most benefit without pervasive accessors.

findings.title: Remove mirrored square Piece storage with a color-tagged slot array
findings.finding: Each square already has a u16 slot into a color-specific Piece list. Eleven slot bits plus one color bit and an empty sentinel could return the Piece via army[slot] without squares:Vec<Option<Piece>>. This saves the full mirrored square array.
findings.limits: get_piece changes from one direct square load to dependent slot/army loads and more bounds checks; random blocker probes may slow. Historical board-direct experiment favored removing this indirection but had inconclusive overall gain. Needs representative reads AND make/remove/clone benchmarks.

findings.title: Position as a single linear u16
findings.finding: Current file:u8,rank:u8 is already2 bytes, so replacing with u16 does not compact Position. It makes to_index trivial but makes file/rank/offset conversion costlier, and can change derived ordering from file-major to rank-major.
findings.limits: Treat as arithmetic tradeoff only; no size win. Piece ordering and sort-dedup order are behavioral constraints. Division by constant36 is normally compiler-strength-reduced; inspect generated code before assuming hardware division. A NonZeroU16 index could shrink Option<Position> from3 to2 bytes through a niche, but plain Position remains2 bytes and the obvious current single-royal cache saving is only2 bytes total.

findings.title: Fixed-size heap square arrays
findings.finding: squares is always1296 entries and piece_slots always1296; Box<[T;1296]> can express fixed shape and remove Vec length/capacity words. Fixed-length arrays may expose more bounds facts to the optimizer. Source-derived header savings are16 bytes for squares Vec→fixed Box and8 bytes for dynamic-slice piece_slots→fixed Box,24 bytes per Board before padding.
findings.limits: Only tens of header bytes are saved; heap payload dominates. Inline Board arrays enlarge stack frames and clones, especially recursive callers. No blanket claim that Box is faster; current owned Vec clone is already contiguous memcpy-compatible.

findings.title: Piece array-of-structs versus struct-of-arrays
findings.finding: Armies are already separated by color. Position-only or type-only scans could read less data with SoA, while complete Piece queries/placements would need multiple arrays and synchronization. Removing redundant per-army color is another small specialization.
findings.limits: Most movement probes consume both type/config and position, so AoS locality is useful. Type count303 makes large per-type side arrays unattractive. Benchmark real scans and swaps rather than assuming SoA wins.

findings.title: Inline common capture deltas with overflow fallback
findings.finding: Most ordinary deltas have zero or one captured Piece yet allocate a Vec on capture. SmallVec-style inline capacity1-4 could avoid common allocations. moved_pieces currently returns a Vec for at most one moved Piece; an Option iterator or slice-shaped accessor is simpler.
findings.limits: Capturing-range rays can remove many pieces, so fixed capacity4 without spill is wrong. Larger inline buffers increase delta size/move costs. affected_pieces_for_attack_detection appears unused outside its own helpers/tests; avoid optimizing dead infrastructure.

findings.title: Allocation-free borrowed board overlays
findings.finding: BoardLike get_pieces_by_color forces owned Vecs for generic attack paths; filtered iterator overlays can avoid base army clones and rebuilding moved/removed entries. Real Board attack path already uses borrowed candidates.
findings.limits: Not a blanket proven engine win. No new borrowed-overlay timing was collected in this sweep. Historical evidence: 20261030 virtual-attack whole-search CPU ratio1.01508;95% source-game cluster interval0.98089..1.06270;36 pairs,6 positions,3 models,2 repetitions. No established whole-workflow gain; API/hypothetical-occupancy microprofile may still improve.

findings.title: Make raw board edits refresh state invariants
findings.finding: Replace raw get_board_mut with an edit operation/guard that commits all state invariants. src/game_state.rs:544 clears eval_inc/nnue but returns &mut Board without updating hash/repetition after caller mutations. Probe moves a Pawn using get_board_mut and confirms hash!=zobrist::compute, while repetition_count still reports 1 for the obsolete hash. Existing production use is limited to bin/test_free_eagle; evaluation tests also use it. Either clearly name this unchecked and force explicit refresh, or provide a closure/RAII guard that refreshes hash and history once after batch edits. Do not recompute per piece in a bulk editor.

findings.title: Share a canonical move-effects description
findings.finding: Share a single move-effects/delta description across application, simulation, capture classification and undo. Today apply_move/execute_single_move, move_to_delta, FreeEagle loops and capture predicates separately encode the same exotic effects. A validated effect record can make parity easier and update hash incrementally in non-search make_move instead of full-board recompute. Avoid replacing cheap make/unmake with per-move Board clones. Need benchmarks to avoid turning a zero-allocation quiet move into effect-vector allocation; generated fixtures already show no current parity mismatch.

findings.title: Consider bounded reachable-form Zobrist tables
findings.finding: Precomputed Zobrist keys versus arithmetic splitmix. src/zobrist.rs deterministically hashes a packed identity on demand. A lookup can replace multiplications, but a full 303-type x2-color x2-promoted x1296-square table is about 12.6 MB before promotion-origin variants. Sparse tables for reachable forms, or a smaller square key combined with piece-form key, deserve a microbenchmark plus representative make/unmake benchmark. Current packing fields are disjoint and includes promotion origin specifically because Whales can move differently. No speed claim and no justification for losing origin metadata or changing identity semantics merely to fit a small chess table.

findings.title: Consider a maintained draw-material class count
findings.finding: Maintain terminal material-class counts only if profiling justifies it. Borrowing army slices removes immediate allocations; maintaining a count of pieces outside the current draw class could turn the scan constant-time and fold into existing board mutation bookkeeping. Additional state/invalidation paths and arbitrary editor snapshots add risk; likely low priority compared with borrowed scans that usually short-circuit early.

findings.title: Separate optional binary snapshot storage from text interchange
findings.finding: Snapshot packing/binary cache is possible for large replay/training datasets. Existing TSFEN sorts and converts piece enums through serde for each token, and snapshot JSON is verbose. Separate text interchange (readable/stable) from optional compact internal snapshot storage. YaneuraOu has PackedSfen; its exact 32-byte representation does not generalize to 804 pieces/303 types/1296 squares. No data-size or I/O bottleneck demonstrated here.

findings.title: Make checked move admission transactional
findings.finding: Public checked move application should be transactional by construction: validate the full route/promotion/effects first, then mutate. Existing checked FreeEagle already does this and has an explicit regression test; checked TwoStep validates both legs before moving. The trusted make_for_search path can partially mutate if deliberately given a malformed multi-leg route with friendly second destination, but its documented contract requires generated legal moves. Do not claim this as a generated-move bug; narrow visibility or a validated-move token could make the contract harder to misuse.

findings.title: Use replay checkpoints for long interactive sessions
findings.finding: apply_live_move applies a move then rebuilds the complete position from its initial/setup root. Navigation also replays from the root. Periodic validated checkpoints or reversible session state could reduce repeated work on long records.
findings.limits: No replay timing collected. Current rebuild is deliberately a reliability mechanism for exotic routes. Checkpoints must preserve turn, draw clock, repetition history, branch structure and any caches; this is not a reason to weaken replay validation.

findings.title: Clarify setup-versus-reset lifecycle semantics
findings.finding: setup_initial_position replaces board and caches and refreshes hash/repetition, but retains existing turn, draw counter and move_history. Current production callsites usually construct a new GameState first. A distinct reset_game operation or explicit precondition would prevent surprising reuse.
findings.limits: Not reproduced as a production failure; do not silently change low-level setup behavior without checking callers.

findings.title: Separate editor side-setting from low-level side toggles
findings.finding: Separate editor side-setting from null-move side-setting. set_current_turn updates hash but not repetition history; calling it on a newly seeded state makes repetition_count report 0. Search null-move callers intentionally push/pop repetition separately, and snapshot loaders reset afterward. Introduce a checked/editor reset operation or document this low-level contract; automatically resetting in the current method would break valid callers. Lower priority than the actual move/import issues.

findings.title: Full conventional magic/PEXT lookup per giant ray
findings.finding: Chess magic tables enumerate relevant occupancy subsets. A36x36 rook has up to70 ray squares, up to68 relevant non-edge blockers, so a direct occupancy-subset table becomes infeasible. Even a single36-square line can have34 relevant bits, over17billion subsets.
findings.limits: Chunked byte tables, segmented bitboards, line bit scans or hyperbola-style arithmetic remain possible; reject the direct one-table transplant, not all hardware bit extraction.

findings.title: Bitboard per piece type and color
findings.finding: 606 full21-word bitboards require101808 bytes before existing board data. Most types are sparse, so copying chess's all-type masks wholesale is expensive compared with compact piece lists. Existing occupied/global-attacker masks and sparse royal index cover useful aggregates.
findings.limits: A few capability groups or active-word masks may help; YaneuraOu explicitly combines movement-equivalent groups to reduce table fetches. Maintaining eight distant-direction indices already screened worse historically.

findings.title: Reject universal bitmap deduplication
findings.finding: Measured slower on Pawn and dense3targetRook;168Bclear/21wordscan dominates tiny lists. Adaptive only.

findings.title: Reject universal sort_unstable replacement
findings.finding: Parity fine but mixed timing: empty Rook~22%slower, some FE no gain; large Tengu/Hook~1.1–1.15x while bitmap~8x. Do not blindly swap every sort.

findings.title: Reject dense type-square-target tables
findings.finding: 303x2x1296x168=131943168B (~125.8MiB) before variants/blocked states/routes. Source-derived estimate, not measured memory. Share movement signatures instead.

findings.title: Keep hypothetical occupancy outside proved narrow cases
findings.finding: Vacated source and first capture matter for Lions/FE/general cases. Original board safe only narrow proven perpendicular RangeRange case.

findings.title: Defer eagerly maintained complete attack maps
findings.finding: Bent sliders/capturing rays are remotely affected by blockers and multicaptures. Eager invalidation cost and correctness complexity; existing target-local candidate masks/direct probes already strong. No measured win.

findings.title: Rejected suspect: unaligned internal path helper call
findings.finding: get_path_positions returns partial normalized diagonal on unaligned input, but current movement callers establish aligned direction. Need reachable invalid-input path before alleging engine bug; is_path_clear rejects nonaligned by running offboard.

findings.title: Preserve legacy raw movement multiplicity
findings.finding: Generator intentionally preserves legacy raw capture duplicates (:490). capability_landing_count used by eval may count them. Removing everywhere can change eval semantics; final target union dedup safely removes already.

findings.title: Rejected suspect: missing generic path victims in FE classifier
findings.finding: move_captures_enemy_piece ignores Standard midpoint captures but all callsites1195/1206/2287 are FE-only. FE ordinary Range=NoJump and sweeps use explicit paths. Non-FE CapturesOnly uses Range visitor with prior-enemy flag. Current RangeRange configs onlyNoJump. No current bug established.

findings.title: Keep all legal promotion choices in the public generator
findings.finding: YaneuraOu intentionally has separate *_ALL modes. Omitting legal underpromotions from public legal API changes behavior/game choices; not parity-preserving efficiency.

findings.title: Keep compact PieceTypeSet rather than HashSet
findings.finding: Capturing blockers already use fiveu64 words and direct bit tests instead of HashSet. Membership tests and Debug compatibility tests exist. An inline u8 group id may reduce descriptor size, but reverting to dynamic hashing has no case here.

findings.title: Pack full Piece identity into u32
findings.finding: 303 current types use9 bits; optional original base uses9 with sentinel511; color1, promoted1, and square11 total31 bits. A spare high-bit sentinel can represent empty without a second tag. All promotion provenance must remain: Whale movement depends on original ReverseChariot and RainDragon on promoted status. Baseline Option<Piece> is already8 bytes, so the1296-square mirror would shrink10368→5184 bytes. Current full-decode prototype was slower: paired median ratio1.34608, range1.18142..1.46146 over nine batches. The tested full-decoding implementation was slower: 4096 mixed square probes median 6408.323 ns current versus 9274.115 ns packed. Reject this decoder; metadata-only compact storage remains a separate possible design.
findings.limits: Prototype safely decodes through ALL_PIECE_TYPES rather than transmuting enum values. It is an independent read-only square store; mutator costs and complete generation are unmeasured. Storing only metadata and using the queried Position may remove index decoding cost. Verdict applies to this full-decode prototype, not every packed layout; memory size alone did not predict speed.

findings.title: Rust inlining, unchecked indexing, target-cpu and SIMD
findings.finding: Release already uses thin LTO and one codegen unit; BoardLike uses generics and can monomorphize, so there is no blanket dynamic-dispatch problem. Position construction/serde is checked, but compiler cannot always infer private-field range. Profile-selected #[inline] or layout tuning is possible; blanket inline(always), unsafe get_unchecked, repr(packed) and SIMD without workload evidence are poor first changes. Actual Piece size8 equals the sum of its current field sizes, so repr(packed) would not even save padding in this structure.
findings.limits: repr(packed) can introduce unaligned access and troublesome references. target-cpu=native reduces binary portability; benefit is workload dependent. Existing historical PGO/native results should inform any followup.

findings.title: Do not transplant endpoint-only Move sentinels or strip provenance
findings.finding: Stockfish/YaneuraOu reserve from==to encodings for special/null moves because ordinary moves do not return to origin. This variant has real capture-and-return routes, and distinct intermediate/path routes with identical endpoints can remove different victims. A compact move must preserve kind, intermediate/full path, promotion and origin; Piece must retain movement-relevant promotion provenance.
findings.limits: Prototype u64 does preserve this information for current generated routes. Simplifying equality/hash to endpoints is a bug, not an optimization.

findings.title: Avoid giant Zobrist lookup tables
findings.finding: Current keys use a cheap deterministic SplitMix64 of packed identity and update incrementally. A naive table covering303 types x304 base choices x2colors x2promoted x1296squares is477513216 entries,3.82GB decimal; allowing all base/origin combinations is mostly unnecessary, and reachable-origin subset is much smaller.
findings.limits: A generated table for only reachable identities could still be benchmarked, but eliminating a few integer multiplies may lose to cache misses. Full keys distinguish promotion origin intentionally; discarding it is a correctness regression.

findings.title: Preserve existing O(1) piece-list removal and royal caches
findings.finding: Board already has u16 square-to-slot index, swap_remove captures, per-color occupied masks, special-global-attacker masks, royal count/sparse positions/single-royal cache and borrowed army access. Replacing these with HashMaps, scanning every square, or repeatedly locating kings would regress established design.
findings.limits: swap_remove changes piece iteration order after captures deliberately; stable-order replacements may change move ordering or cost. Current tests cover index/cache consistency.

findings.title: Preserve this variant's royal-capture legality semantics
findings.finding: Do not import chess pin/self-check legality or single-king loss assumptions. This engine intentionally generates pseudo-legal moves and loses when all King/CrownPrince royals are gone; same-side royals can coexist. is_legal_move_assuming_reachable's optional self-check path is not enabled by normal generation. A chess-style blanket king-safety filter would change game rules and search move choice, outside optimization scope.

findings.title: Do not import ordinary-shogi hand/drop/repetition rules
findings.finding: Do not import standard-shogi drops, nifu, pawn-drop mate, perpetual-check adjudication, or YaneuraOu's fourfold repetition as automatic fixes. No captures-to-hand/drop system exists here; current fivefold/progress/custom insufficient-material rules are explicit. Historical variant rule verification would be a separate task.

findings.title: Use spill-capable capture and move buffers
findings.finding: Do not cap capture logs at one/two victims or board/move capacity at chess MAX_MOVES=256. Sweeping and multi-leg moves, 1296 squares and hundreds of pieces require spill-capable storage and data-driven capacity checks. Do not infer clone cost from Board's 824-byte header; most storage is heap owned.

findings.title: Preserve collision-safe repetition prefix indexing
findings.finding: Do not replace existing repeated-key prefix indexing with a HashMap automatically. RepetitionPrefix uses sorted counts plus a low-bit presence filter, with collision-safe full-key binary search and suffix scanning; it already addresses long histories without per-move map updates. Existing test suite covers shortening prefix, collisions and independent clones. Profiling needed for alternative structures. Truncating repetition history on any progress counter reset imports assumptions that require proof for all exotic movement/promotion states.

findings.title: Avoid full-board clone as the default simulation primitive
findings.finding: Full board clone per simulated move is rejected as default direction. Existing virtual boards/make-unmake already avoid copying 1296 squares plus lists and indices. Their local allocation issues can be targeted without reverting to copy/make.

recommended_sequence: Fix reproduced state/interchange issues in focused PRs: Free Eagle final history leg, promotion admission, restore cache invalidation, legacy coordinate validation and documented TM1 routes.
Take low-risk allocation wins next: borrowed terminal/snapshot APIs, bulk validated snapshot construction, residual fixed direction arrays and target-only dead path storage.
Integrate one generation change at a time: perpendicular second rays first, then adaptive target bitmap/streamed multi-leg output. Preserve route/progress effects and ordered move results.
Trial Copy inline Move before pervasive bit packing; benchmark complete generation/apply/clone workloads with realistic games. Packed Piece full decoding already lost the local comparison.
Treat line occupancy, compiled movement signatures, selective caches and alternate layouts as experiments requiring update-cost and integrated parity measurements.
confidence: 12,461 sampled generated moves passed validated/trusted application, simulation, full-hash and undo checks. Movement comparisons passed 401,186 directed reach, 144,048 candidate-filter and 134,784 specialized-probe checks. Turn prototype passed 1,152 ordered target-list cases; line prototype passed 31,104 rook counts; representation checks passed 387 move roundtrips, 18,180 piece roundtrips, 4,096 square reads and 16 draw/snapshot cases. These checks share movement configurations and are not an independent historical-rules oracle. No long-game randomized differential, sanitizer/Miri campaign, fuzz campaign, integrated performance confirmation or playing-strength experiment was run. The generated samples are moves, not independent games. Undo checks compare square contents, turn, counter, hash and current repetition count; they do not prove restoration of piece-list order or byte-identical history. Evaluator caches were unbound during the broad state sample.

sources.idea: The chess move uses 16 bits. Taikyoku needs 11 bits per square and route identity; our safe complete-move prototype uses 64 bits.

sources.label: Stockfish: state and attacks

sources.label: Stockfish: architecture-specific slider techniques
sources.idea: Contemporary source contains multiple slider techniques rather than one universal magic implementation. Per-line arithmetic is the more plausible adaptation to 36x36.

sources.label: YaneuraOu: generation modes
sources.idea: Target bitboards, caller output and specialized generation modes are applicable ideas. Modes that omit promotion choices cannot replace an all-legal-moves API.

sources.label: YaneuraOu: Move16 and Move32
sources.idea: Separate compact internal moves from richer execution metadata. Its no-op/null sentinels are unsafe to copy when real capture-and-return moves exist.

sources.label: YaneuraOu: state and board groups
sources.idea: Caller-owned StateInfo, distinct checked/trusted move contracts, selected movement groups and packed interchange offer design ideas without importing standard-shogi rules.

sources.label: YaneuraOu: multiword bitboards
sources.idea: Its two-word 81-square representation illustrates adapting bitboard width to a board. Our board requires 21 u64 words; line-local masks avoid scanning all 21 for simple rays.

sources.label: Fairy-Stockfish: generalized riders and leapers
sources.idea: Shared rider/leaper classes and variant masks suggest compiling by movement signature. Dense tables still become large for 303 types and 1296 squares.

sources.label: Arasan programmer guide
sources.idea: Its square array plus bitboards, 64-bit move records and saved reversible state show that hybrid layouts and richer compact moves are viable alternatives to a single representation.

sources.label: Rust type-layout reference
sources.idea: Actual sizes were measured with rustc 1.92.0 rather than assumed. Rust layout is not a stable serialization format; packed/niche representations need explicit safe conversion.
